name: Lisp
typeSystem: The original Lisp was dynamically typed; the broader Lisp family now includes dynamically typed dialects such as Common Lisp and Scheme as well as statically typed descendants.
runtime: Lisp denotes a language family rather than one modern runtime. Early Lisp had both interpreters and compilers; current dialects use implementations ranging from interpreters and bytecode virtual machines to native-code compilers.

runtimes.name: Lisp 1.5 interpreter
runtimes.role: Historical implementation described in the Lisp 1.5 Programmer's Manual.

compilers.name: Lisp 1.5 compiler
compilers.role: Historical compiler described alongside the interpreter in the Lisp 1.5 system.

concurrencyModel: No single model applies to the Lisp family; concurrency facilities vary by dialect and implementation.
